rationale:
## Judgment
The structures and model-reference behavior largely match `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure`, but required test coverage has a traceability gap.

## Obligations and implementation
The schema's individual fields and properties impose the following obligations (grouped here by structure, rather than treating whole structures as single obligations):

- User configuration: optional default, named configuration map, and project-selection map. Workspace configuration: optional default, configuration map, and an empty map when that map is omitted. These are implemented by `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]` and `src/config.rs#struct[WorkspaceAuthoringConfig]`. `src/config.rs#struct[ProjectSelection]` supplies the selection's configuration name. Tests include `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it]`.
- Authoring configuration: backend, optional positive concurrency, and optional policy. The backend must be a flattened tagged union with Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI variants; policy must have the two stated lowercase TOML forms. These are implemented by `src/config.rs#struct[AuthoringConfig]`, `src/config.rs#enum[BackendConfig]`, and `src/config.rs#enum[AssessmentPolicy]`, reachable through the marked configuration types. Tests include `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]`, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]`.
- Bedrock: model, optional AWS profile, optional region, optional credentials, and options map. Credentials: access-key ID, secret access key, and optional session token. Ollama: model, optional endpoint, optional environment-variable name, optional secret key, and options map. OpenAI: optional model, optional endpoint, optional environment-variable name, optional secret key, and options map. These fields are supplied by `src/config.rs#struct[BedrockConfig]`, `src/config.rs#struct[BedrockCredentials]`, `src/config.rs#struct[OllamaConfig]`, and `src/config.rs#struct[OpenAiConfig]`. The round-trip tests above, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` exercise their representation.
- Options must support strings, booleans, integers, finite floats, recursive arrays, and recursive string-keyed maps. `src/config.rs#enum[OptionValue]` supplies the variants; `src/config.rs#impl[OptionValue]/fn[validate]` recursively rejects nonfinite floats. The backend round-trip test covers the valid forms, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` covers nonfinite scalar, array, and map values.
- Secrets must serialize normally and redact Debug output. The transparent `src/config.rs#struct[SecretString]` and marked `src/config.rs#impl[SecretString/fmt::Debug]/fn[fmt]` implement these separately; the explicit-credentials round-trip/redaction test asserts both.
- Default policy must be Once for OpenAI and Confirm otherwise. `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[effective_policy]` implements this. The policy round-trip test covers the non-OpenAI default; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_policy_defaults_to_once_without_changing_explicit_policy]` covers OpenAI.
- Effective defaults must be the stated Ollama endpoint, OpenAI endpoint, OpenAI key-variable name, and OpenAI model. The marked endpoint methods and `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[api_key_from]`, together with reachable `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[model]`, implement these. The backend round-trip test, OpenAI credential-resolution test, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_defaults_are_effective_only_and_explicit_values_win]` assert the defaults.
- ModelRef must contain backend kind and model ID, derive from the selected backend, preserve the exact identifier, and leave connection settings intact. `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[model_ref]` reaches `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[model_ref]` and `src/config.rs#struct[ModelRef]`. The map round-trip test checks exact Bedrock identifiers and retained profile/region, and exact Ollama tags with retained endpoint. The OpenAI configuration test checks its backend kind and exact explicit ID; the OpenAI defaults test checks its effective default ID.

## Gap
`src/config.rs#impl[OllamaConfig]/fn[endpoint]` has separate effective-output paths for an omitted endpoint and an explicit endpoint. The subject specifies an optional endpoint with a default, so both paths require tests. The subject-marked backend round-trip test asserts only the default result. The subject-marked map round-trip test checks the explicit stored field, but does not call `endpoint()` on that configuration.

The explicit effective-endpoint assertion does exist in `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]`, which calls `endpoint()` and asserts `http://server:11434`. However, that test has no `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure`; it was found only by searching outside the subject's marked tests. Under the required test-reference rule, this is a gap: that test should carry the subject reference (or an appropriately marked test should cover the explicit endpoint path). No testing exemption applies to this conditional endpoint selection, and no supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges the gap.

rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

- **Confirm a first `true` assessment in an independent second conversation.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` calls `assess` again with fresh sources; `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` creates a new request and conversation-local state. Covered by `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` and `fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]` in that file.
- **Confirm a first FIXME assessment independently.** The same code handles this, covered by `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]`.
- **Treat equal outcome kinds as agreement and record the first assessment.** `assess_subject` compares `kind()` and returns `first`; the agreeing-assessments test checks distinct FIXME acknowledgments and rationales, and the citation test checks `true` agreement.
- **On disagreement, verify the less favorable assessment in a third independent conversation under `requirements.authoring.verifier_prompt`.** `assess_subject`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[favorability]`, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[verify]` implement selection and verification. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[disagreeing_assessments_verify_the_less_favorable_one]` checks third-conversation prompts, tools, and selection for `true` versus `false` and `true` versus FIXME.
- **Order `false` below FIXME and FIXME below `true`.** `favorability` assigns ranks 0, 1, and 2. The FIXME/`true` ordering is tested, but the `false`/FIXME ordering lacks the required outcome assertion (gap below).
- **Record the outcome derived under `requirements.authoring.verifier_outcome`.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[confirmed_record]` applies the verification result. The disagreeing-assessments test checks real/unacknowledged, real/acknowledged, and unreal gaps.
- **For sites, treat differing `applies` values as disagreement and regard `applies: true` as less favorable.** `assess_subject` and `favorability` implement these decisions; `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_assessments_differing_only_in_applies_are_verified]` covers both orders and recorded applicability.
- **State the disagreement and verification conclusion in the recorded rationale.** `confirmed_record` appends both. The disagreement and site tests assert the resulting rationale. `src/commands.rs#fn[disagreements]` exposes recorded disagreements for review, tested by `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_lists_definitions_and_reviews_whose_assessments_disagreed]`.
- **Give each conversation its own usage record.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[followup_log]` starts follow-up logs. The agreement, disagreement, citation, and batch tests assert separate records.
- **Confirm selected citation reviews with their target as subject.** The common `assess_subject` path does this; `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]` checks the targeted fresh prompts and usage records.
- **Confirm selected site reviews with their target as subject.** The same path does this; the site-assessments test checks agreement, disagreement, and the verifier's site target.

## Unacknowledged gaps

1. **Missing test for the explicitly stated `false`-below-FIXME ordering.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[favorability]` implements this ordering, but none of the subject-marked tests exercises a first FIXME assessment followed by `false` and asserts that verification receives the `false` assessment. The disagreement table tests only `true`/`false` and FIXME/`true`. This is a named ordering obligation, not a demand for every combination of unspecified branches; its conditional ranking and selection need a test.

2. **The adaptive confirmation path's test lacks a reference to this subject.** `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]`, reached through `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]`, separately implements confirmation, agreement, disagreement selection, and verification. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_sol_failure_is_final_and_confirm_uses_sol_verification]` exercises that separate path and asserts its verification-derived record and visible disagreement, but carries test references only to adaptive, persistence, and policy. It needs a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.confirmation`; none of the supplied subject-marked tests exercises that adaptive path.

No `{fixme}` acknowledgment of these gaps was found in the subject references or inspected sources.

rationale:
## Judgment

The implementation substantially fulfills `requirements.authoring.credentials`, but a named credential boundary lacks a test.

## Obligation mapping

- **Reject Bedrock credentials combined with `aws_profile`.** `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]`, reached from both marked `parse` methods, performs this check. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them]` tests rejection.
- **Reject Ollama `api_key` combined with `api_key_env`.** The same validator implements this; the same test exercises it.
- **Reject OpenAI `api_key` combined with `api_key_env`.** The validator has an OpenAI check, exercised by `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]`.
- **Pass explicit credentials directly to the selected provider.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider]/fn[connect]` passes the OpenAI and Ollama keys to their provider builders. Its Bedrock path reaches `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[bedrock_sdk_loader]`, which supplies an SDK credentials provider. The marked Bedrock SDK test asserts all three values; `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_key_only_profile_defaults_to_sol_and_accepts_overrides]` assert authentication headers for the other providers.
- **Do not change process environment variables; do not write credential files.** These provider paths only read saved fields or resolve environment values and configure provider objects. They contain no environment mutation or credential-file writing operation. These negative properties have no separate conditional or transformation requiring a test; the workspace CLI test additionally asserts that configuration files remain unchanged and no user configuration appears.
- **Round-trip saved explicit values.** The configuration types use `Serialize` and `Deserialize`, including transparent `SecretString`. The marked explicit-credentials round-trip test checks equality after serialization and parsing for all providers.
- **Do not serialize profile-resolved credentials; do not serialize environment-resolved credentials.** SDK credentials are held separately from the saved `BedrockConfig`; the API-key resolution methods return values without modifying configuration. The saved types serialize only their saved fields. The marked Ollama authentication test and OpenAI configuration test assert that resolved environment keys are absent from serialization. Profile resolution similarly has no operation inserting its result into a saved configuration.
- **Exclude credential values from debug output.** `src/config.rs#impl[SecretString/fmt::Debug]/fn[fmt]` emits a fixed marker. The marked round-trip/debug test checks all five explicit credential fields.
- **Exclude credential values from configuration diagnostics.** `src/config.rs#fn[decode]` removes decoder source input and replaces collected credential values in messages; validation messages do not interpolate values. The marked diagnostic tests exercise malformed and wrongly typed credential settings.
- **Do not echo credential-containing source lines in TOML diagnostics.** `src/config.rs#fn[parse_document]` reports only syntax position. The marked explicit-credentials diagnostic test exercises malformed credential-bearing TOML through both user and workspace parsers.
- **Exclude credential values from usage records.** `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]` and its component types store metadata rather than credentials or source bodies. The marked Ollama workspace CLI test and OpenAI CLI test assert that their literal keys are absent from usage JSON.
- **Exclude credential values from initial prompts; redact configuration source values under `requirements.authoring.redaction`.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[initial_prompt]` consumes model-facing inputs, and `src/redaction.rs#impl[Redaction]/fn[of_file]` applies configuration-field redaction, replacing invalid TOML wholesale. The marked model-input/read/search test verifies prompt secrecy and redacted configuration reads; `src/redaction/tests.rs#fn[configuration_credential_fields_are_redacted_by_name_whatever_their_values]` asserts named-field replacements. The workspace CLI test also asserts that its literal key is absent from the model request body. I have not reassessed the separate redaction requirement.
- **Report indexed credential-bearing workspace files; name the file; name the credential fields; recommend credential-source references.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_committed_credentials]` implements each property. Its marked committed/untracked workspace test asserts the report, path, field names, recommendations, and absence of secret values, including the staging boundary.
- **Discourage literal workspace credentials; recommend AWS profiles; recommend environment-variable references.** The marked documentation sections in `md/reference.md#section[How%20it%20works]/section[Authoring%20evidence%20with%20a%20model]` and `md/requirements/authoring.md#section[Authoring%20evidence]/section[Configuration]/section[Editing%20the%20file]` do so directly.
- **Use placeholders in examples; explain possible commitment of workspace files; explain source reads when allowed.** Those sections provide uppercase credential placeholders, explain their substitution, warn about version control, and describe redacted model reads. These are documentary obligations carried out directly by text, requiring no execution test.

## Unacknowledged testing gap

The supported Bedrock credential form explicitly names **nonempty `access_key_id`**, a boundary implemented by `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]`. However, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them]` tests empty `secret_access_key` and empty `session_token`, but not empty `access_key_id`. I inspected the supplied credential tests and searched the tests for an empty-access-key case without finding one. The successful Bedrock SDK test uses a nonempty access key and does not verify this rejection boundary.

The permission to supply credentials does not require exercising the permission itself, but the explicitly named nonempty boundary of that supported input needs a rejection test under the task's testing rules. No network, elapsed-time, or process-state setup is needed to test it through either parser. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges this missing test.

rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

The implementation substantially carries out `requirements.authoring.file_discovery`, but required test coverage has gaps.

1. **Expose `list_files` with the stated interface**, including an optional string path defaulting to `.` and entries with string paths and file/directory kinds: `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[optional_path]`, and `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[list_files]` implement this. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts the file-entry shape; `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[failed_listings_return_explanatory_tool_errors]` checks invalid arguments. Root-listing tests exercise the default path.
2. **List immediate children of the requested directory:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[list_files]` uses `read_dir`, without recursive enumeration. The reading test above asserts a requested `src` listing; `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]` asserts root children rather than their descendants.
3. **Return project-relative paths where possible:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[relative_path]` strips the root prefix. Both preceding tests assert relative paths.
4. **Return absolute paths for permitted external files:** the same helper preserves external absolute paths, and `list_files` applies it to directory children. **Coverage gap:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not]` asserts that the external directory is exposed at the root and that external files can be searched and read, but never lists that permitted directory and asserts its child's absolute path. None of the subject-marked tests supplies that missing listing assertion. This filesystem behavior is not exempt from testing.
5. **Expose available generated-output directories at the root:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[list_files]` appends `SourceAccess::extra_roots`, defined at `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[extra_roots]`. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files]` asserts the generated directory appears, and disappears when disallowed.
6. **Expose configured external allow paths at the root:** the same extra-root loop implements this; the allowed/external test identified above asserts the external directory's absolute path appears.
7. **Return explanatory errors on failed listings:** `src/authoring/access.rs#fn[resolve]` explains resolution failures; `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[list_files]` explains enumeration failures. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[failed_listings_return_explanatory_tool_errors]` asserts errors for missing paths, a file requested as a directory, and malformed arguments.
8. **Apply `requirements.authoring.read_denial` to denied access:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[project_path]` invokes `SourceAccess::path`; `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` returns dispatch failures as tool errors and continues without adding inputs. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_untracked_reads_return_an_untracked_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` exercises an explicitly denied directory listing, checks the explanation, continued assessment, and absence of denied evidence.
9. **Never make directory listings evidence inputs:** `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[array]` sets `evidence` false, and `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[delivered]` consequently returns no inputs. The reading test asserts an ordinary listing's inputs are empty. **Coverage/reference gap:** this obligation also governs the separate paged delivery path in `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]`. `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order]` exercises paged directory listings and asserts each page has no inputs, but lacks a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.file_discovery`. No subject-marked test covers that path. Paging itself is specified by `requirements.authoring.result_pages`; it is not an unspecified feature.
10. **Omit files excluded under `requirements.authoring.source_tools`:** `list_files` filters each candidate through `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]`. Subject-marked tests cover evidence-directory exclusion and its symlink aliases (`generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery`), outside symlinks (`outside_symlinks_are_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery`), untracked files (`git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files`), and alias/target index eligibility (`git_symlink_reads_require_both_the_alias_and_target_to_be_tracked`), all under `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]`.
11. **In Git, list directories only with eligible source descendants, except allowed/generated directories:** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` calls `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[has_source_under]`, which checks eligible tracked descendants and extra roots. The Git-tools test asserts that a tracked-source directory appears and an untracked-only directory does not; the allowed/external and Cargo-output tests exercise the exceptions.
12. **Treat explicitly requested excluded paths as denials:** the initial `project_path` check rejects them rather than silently filtering the requested directory. Evidence-directory, untracked-directory, disallowed-directory, and generated-directory tests identified above exercise this, with the CLI test verifying continuation.

All implementation locations above are marked roots or reachable through their calls and types. The two identified testing gaps are not acknowledged by a supplied `{fixme}` reference. Therefore the requirement does not fully satisfy the review rules.

rationale:
## Judgment

`requirements.authoring.github_reads` has unacknowledged gaps in mandatory caching and in testing missing-issue staleness.

## Obligations and coverage

1. **Expose `github` with the stated argument interface.** `src/github.rs#fn[tool_definition]`, included by `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]`, declares the interface; `src/github.rs#fn[tool]` enforces it. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts exposure, and `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[the_tool_reads_issues_with_the_token_and_redacts_bodies]` exercises dispatch semantics.
2. **Return the issue reference.** `src/github.rs#fn[tool]` returns the requested reference; the latter unit test asserts it.
3. **Return an open/closed state.** The same implementation and test cover both states.
4. **Return a string title.** The same implementation and test assert the returned title.
5. **Return a string body.** The same implementation and test exercise the body, also covered by `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_successful_github_read_records_no_evidence_inputs]`.
6. **Require `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`.** `src/github.rs#fn[tool]` uses `src/fixme.rs#fn[is_issue_reference]`; the tool unit test rejects malformed references.
7. **Read issues or pull requests through the GitHub API.** `src/github.rs#impl[Client]/fn[fetch_all]` builds the issue API endpoint and calls `src/github.rs#fn[fetch]`. The tool unit test asserts the GET path. This endpoint also serves pull requests; no separate implementation path is introduced.
8. **Authenticate using `GITHUB_TOKEN` when set.** `src/github.rs#impl[GithubIssues]/fn[from_env]` resolves the token, and `src/github.rs#fn[fetch]` applies bearer authentication. The tool unit test asserts the authorization header with an injected token. Direct environment resolution has no dedicated test, but qualifies for the process-environment exemption: the project search found no test setting `GITHUB_TOKEN` for these reads.
9. **Apply `requirements.authoring.redaction` to the returned body.** `src/github.rs#fn[fetch]` calls `redact_text` before constructing the result or caching it. The tool unit test asserts removal of a secret from both the returned body and cache. This checks application of the cited requirement, not its redaction algorithm anew.
10. **Do not record GitHub results as evidence inputs.** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` returns an empty input list for GitHub. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_successful_github_read_records_no_evidence_inputs]` asserts both that list and unchanged recorded inputs.
11. **Do not let GitHub read results make evidence stale.** Those results introduce no evidence dependency; the same unchanged-input assertion covers that exclusion. The separately required FIXME-state invalidation is handled explicitly below.
12. **Route every GitHub read through one cache under the configured state root.** Tool reads, mandatory-input lookups, and issue findings all use `GithubIssues::read_all`. `src/github.rs#impl[GithubIssues]/fn[from_env]` selects the `github` state subdirectory. The integration test `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[closing_an_acknowledged_issue_makes_the_fixme_record_stale_and_reassessed]` asserts its location and reuse across author/status invocations. **However, the cache is optional in production, as detailed below.**
13. **Key the cache by issue.** `src/github.rs#impl[Client]/fn[cache_path]` derives owner/repository/number filenames, and `src/github.rs#impl[Client]/fn[cached]` checks the issue. `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[results_are_cached_by_issue_for_an_hour_and_failures_are_not]` exercises separate issues and cached outcomes.
14. **Reuse results less than one hour old instead of contacting GitHub.** `src/github.rs#impl[Client]/fn[cached]` checks the timestamp against the 3,600-second `CACHE_LIFETIME`; `read_all` fetches only misses. The cache unit test asserts reuse and expiry at an hour, and the integration test asserts no additional request for a fresh cached state.
15. **Return an explanatory error for a malformed reference.** `src/github.rs#fn[tool]` does so; the tool unit test asserts the explanation.
16. **Return an explanatory error for a missing issue.** The same function and test cover the missing-issue result.
17. **Return an explanatory error for a failed request.** The same function and test cover HTTP failure and an unreachable endpoint.
18. **Look up each issue named by a mandatory input's `{fixme}`.** `src/github.rs#fn[input_issue_states]`, using `fixme_issues` and `input_ranges`, collects and reads those issues. Preparation in `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_site]` invokes it. `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[inputs_containing_fixmes_carry_their_issue_states]` checks multiple issues and different input ranges.
19. **Supply each state with its input as open or closed.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[model_mandatory_inputs]` adds `github_issues`; initial and verification prompts use that representation. The input-state unit test checks state values, and the CLI integration test asserts the state-bearing model prompt.
20. **Assume open when GitHub cannot be reached.** `src/github.rs#impl[IssueRead]/fn[state]` implements this. The tool, input-state, and issue-findings unit tests exercise offline/unreachable behavior.
21. **Do not record those supplied states.** Model inputs are decorated clones, not recorded inputs. Both cited integration tests assert that evidence and usage omit `github_issues`.
22. **Have status treat a FIXME determination as stale when an acknowledging issue is closed.** `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` calls `src/github.rs#fn[add_issue_findings]`. The batch integration test asserts the stale finding and invalid status.
23. **Have author treat that closed-issue determination as stale.** `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]` and `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[subject_is_current]` apply the same findings before freshness decisions. The batch integration test asserts reassessment.
24. **Apply that staleness rule when an acknowledging issue does not exist.** `src/github.rs#impl[IssueRead]/fn[not_open]` and `src/github.rs#fn[add_issue_findings]` implement it, but the required missing-issue staleness outcome is not tested; see below.
25. **For site reviews, use the `{fixme}` references inside the site.** The site loop in `src/github.rs#fn[add_issue_findings]` does this. `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_closed_issue_of_a_fixme_inside_a_site_makes_only_its_site_review_stale]` asserts site staleness without staling the requirement record.
26. **Repository validation must not perform this GitHub-dependent staleness check.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_repository]` uses repository inspection without adding GitHub findings. The batch integration test asserts validation still accepts the record and makes no additional GitHub requests.

The optional local API override is constrained by `src/github.rs#fn[is_loopback_api_url]`; `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_loopback_api_urls_with_a_port_are_accepted]` covers accepted and rejected forms.

## Gaps

- **Caching can silently be bypassed.** `src/github.rs#impl[GithubIssues]/fn[from_env]` converts an unavailable state root, or a state root inside the project, into `cache: None` while retaining a live API client. `src/github.rs#impl[Client]/fn[store]` also discards directory/write/persist failures. Consequently a successful GitHub read can be returned without entering the required shared cache, and another read within an hour contacts GitHub again. The subject requires every read to go through the state-root cache, without an uncached fallback. The same items mark `requirements.configuration.state_location`, whose supplied text requires reporting state-location/write failures rather than silently proceeding; it does not authorize this fallback.
- **Missing-issue staleness lacks an outcome test.** In `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closed_and_missing_issues_fail_their_fixmes_items_and_acknowledged_records]`, the missing issue is `o/r#3`, but `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[project]` puts it in an unnamed declaration FIXME. The recorded determination acknowledges `o/r#1`, which is closed, not missing. Thus the test checks missing-issue diagnostics but only closed-issue record staleness. The other referenced staleness tests likewise use a closed issue. No referenced test asserts that a recorded FIXME acknowledging a nonexistent issue becomes stale. This is an expressly named failure case, executable with the existing local-server fixtures, so no testing exemption applies.

No `{fixme}` acknowledgment of either gap was supplied or found among the subject's references.

rationale:
## Obligation and implementation

`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules` has one MUST obligation: every assessment prompt must replace `{{judgment_rules}}` with the exact supplied text. The quoted rules are the content to insert, not additional obligations for the Rust code to perform judgments itself.

The implementation meets this obligation: `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[approved_text]` extracts the approved block directly from the book, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[shared_blocks]` associates it with `judgment_rules`. Both `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[initial_prompt]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[verification_prompt]` supply that association to `Prompt::filled`. The reachable `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[Prompt]/fn[filled]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[fill]` insert the block without transforming its content. The initial, citation, site, and verifier templates in `requirements.authoring.initial_prompt`, `requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`, `requirements.authoring.site_prompt`, and `requirements.authoring.verifier_prompt` all contain the placeholder. Their other prompt content is specified by those requirements.

## Test coverage and gap

The marked tests in `src/authoring/mod.rs` assert the complete approved rules block for ordinary initial prompts (`mod[tests]/fn[initial_prompt_carries_the_review_criteria]`), citation prompts (`mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]`), site prompts (`mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]`), requirement verification (`mod[tests]/fn[disagreeing_assessments_verify_the_less_favorable_one]`), and example/citation verification (`mod[tests]/fn[verifier_prompts_name_examples_and_citation_reviews]`).

**Unacknowledged testing gap:** the distinct site-verification path in `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[verification_prompt]` has no subject-marked test asserting that its output includes the approved judgment rules. The located site-verification test, `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_assessments_differing_only_in_applies_are_verified]`, exercises that path but neither asserts the judgment-rules block nor carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`. Its assertion that no `{{` remains does not establish that the required text is present. This output path needs an assertion of the approved rules and the subject reference. No applicable acknowledgment was supplied or found in the sources read.

rationale:
## Obligation coverage

- **Reject, rather than accept, the first otherwise-valid sole submission citing line numbers, and continue the conversation**, for both judgment submissions and `submit_verification`: `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` checks submission count and parsing before invoking `Rejection::decide`; its rejection branch returns an error tool result and continues. `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[decide]` applies the cited detection behavior and tracks the first rejection. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[verify]` routes verification submissions through this same conversation implementation.
- **Quote the matched text**: `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[decide]` includes the debug-quoted match in the rejection message.
- **Repeat the judgment rules' location guidance**: `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[location_guidance]` extracts that guidance, and `converse` supplies it to `decide` for inclusion in the tool result.
- **Give a fresh random UUID**: `decide` generates a new version-4 UUID for the rejection.
- **Say the model may submit once more**, **without line numbers**, or **with `rationale` exactly the UUID to retain the rejected submission**: the rejection message in `decide` explicitly explains each alternative.
- **Count the rejection in usage like other turns**: `converse` records the request and its completion, records the rejected tool invocation, and saves usage before continuing.

`src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]` exercises rejection, quoted matches, guidance inclusion, UUID parsing and freshness, and retaining the original submission. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rationale_citing_line_numbers_is_rejected_once]` exercises conversation continuation, guidance delivery, resubmission alternatives, and two recorded usage requests. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rationale_without_line_numbers_is_accepted_at_once]` covers immediate acceptance of a clean rationale. The additional resubmission behavior is specified by `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission`.

## Unacknowledged testing gap

The explicitly named **`submit_verification` case has no test carrying a reference to this requirement**. All supplied rejection tests exercise `submit_judgment`: the direct unit test names that tool, and the integration tests use `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/impl[ResubmittingProvider/CompletionProvider]`, which hard-codes `submit_judgment`. Thus none tests rejection and continuation for an otherwise-valid verification submission, including delivery of the correctly named retry instruction and usage accounting in that case.

The implementation is shared, but the requirement explicitly names verification as a separate condition requiring coverage. This is not a pass-through or external-state exemption: the rejection logic makes conditional decisions and constructs a tool-specific result. Add a referenced test exercising `converse` with `submit_verification` (or `verify`) and asserting that outcome. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap.

rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

1. **Construct each assessment's mandatory set by combining applicable contributions.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[sources]` dispatches to `prepare`, `prepare_citation`, and `prepare_site` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`. These assemble the subject-specific selectors and terminology dependencies. Definition and citation assembly are exercised by `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_review_inputs_combine_item_declarations_terms_and_built_ins_once]`. Site assembly has the coverage limitation below.
2. **Contributing requirements must cite this requirement.** The contributing texts in `requirements.authoring_input`, `requirements.examples.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.references.citation_review`, and `requirements.references.site_review` do so.
3. **Those requirements must define which sources contribute.** Those texts identify declarations, reference targets, outline nodes, citation commentary, built-ins, and terminology dependencies.
4. **Those requirements must define when they contribute.** They distinguish requirement, example, citation, and site assessments and terminology introduced by contributed inputs. These textual obligations need no runtime test.
5. **Include every applicable contribution.** The three preparation methods implement the separate contribution paths, with `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[definition_inputs]` adding terminology. The definition and citation tests above assert combined contents; the site-path gap is detailed below.
6. **Deduplicate identical selections.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[insert_selector]`, the dependency containment checks, and the built-in containment checks perform deduplication. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` checks identical implementation/test anchors yield one input; the citation combination test checks repeated declarations, a shared term, and a repeated built-in occur once.
7. **Report unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[source_input]` propagates access and resolution errors; preparation precedes provider connection in `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]`. Tests include `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[unresolvable_mandatory_inputs_fail_before_any_model_request]`.
8. **Supply the complete set in the initial model request.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[initial_prompt]` serializes `model_mandatory_inputs`; `assess` passes that prompt to `converse`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` checks the definition request; `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` check their respective initial requests.
9. **Omit default-excluded project-root evidence output.** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[omit_generated_evidence]` and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[generated_evidence_selector]` filter these selections during definition preparation. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_references_are_omitted_by_default]` and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_anchors_are_omitted_unless_allowed_and_abort_when_disallowed]` assert omission.
10. **Include symlink aliases in that omission.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[generated_evidence_path]` checks canonical paths; the generated-evidence anchor test exercises an alias on Unix.
11. **Permit explicitly allowed evidence selections.** The omission predicate consults policy allow rules, and `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` accepts allowed paths. The generated-evidence anchor test asserts inclusion after an explicit allow.
12. **Abort explicitly disallowed selections under `requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.** The omission predicate does not suppress an explicit denial; `SourceAccess::path` returns it through preparation before inference. The generated-evidence anchor test asserts the denied evidence path and permission error. This applies the cited denial requirement without reassessing its independent implementation obligations.

## Unacknowledged testing gap

The obligation to combine **every applicable contribution for each assessment** is not fully tested on the site-review path. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_site]` has its own loop that selects declarations cited by the site's requirement, followed by terminology dependency assembly. However, the subject-linked site test, `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]`, asserts a mandatory set of exactly two inputs: the site and its requirement. It does not exercise or assert inclusion of a cited declaration or terminology in a site assessment. The other subject-linked combination tests run `prepare` or `prepare_citation`, not this separate assembly path.

A subject-linked site test must exercise and assert those applicable contributions (and their delivery in the initial set). This code performs conditional selection and transformation, so the testing exemption does not apply. No supplied or discovered `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap.

rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

`requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers` imposes four obligations: omit project-source line numbers and ranges from (1) prompts, (2) tool results, and (3) tool errors, subject to its quoted-source and supplied-number exceptions; and (4) identify source locations using files and outline selectors under `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.

- **Prompts:** `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_model_input]` and its reachable `to_input` serialize source inputs as file, selector, hash, kind, and quoted text, without numerical locations. `src/sites.rs#impl[SiteItem]/fn[matches_value]` similarly serializes query matches using selectors. The marked tests `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` check root inputs and site-prompt locations respectively.
- **Tool results:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[outline_entries]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[references]`, and `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]` emit selectors rather than numerical locations. The marked tests `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs`, `references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs`, `search_merges_context_windows_and_respects_ignore_rules`, and `separate_windows_in_one_node_are_divided_by_an_elision_line` in `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]` assert these result forms. Its marked `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes` tests verify selector-based read results, including range reads.
- **Tool errors:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` applies `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#fn[without_source_lines]` to dispatch errors. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[read_lines]` repeats only the requested numbers for invalid ranges. The marked `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error]` checks parser and diagnostic forms and both supplied-number forms; `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_give_the_model_no_line_numbers_it_did_not_supply]` checks actual delivery of a sanitized parse error.

## Gaps

1. **Error locations lose their numerical coordinates without receiving outline selectors.** `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#fn[without_source_lines]` transforms, for example, a duplicate-declaration diagnostic into `md/b.md: duplicate requirement r; first declared at md/a.md`. Those are source locations identified only by files, not files and selectors as the second sentence requires. Its marked unit test explicitly asserts this output, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` delivers the sanitized string unchanged. Removing numbers fulfills the prohibition but not the replacement-location obligation. The sanitizer has no source-resolution mechanism to supply the missing selectors.

2. **The violation-match output path lacks a subject-marked test.** `src/sites.rs#impl[SiteItem]/fn[matches_value]` has separate site-match and violation-match output paths. The supplied subject-marked site-prompt test exercises the former. Tests exercising the latter exist at `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[violation_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` and `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[sites_are_the_innermost_nodes_of_site_matches_and_violations_within_them]`; the latter asserts the complete selector-based, number-free violation result. Neither carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers`. This separate governed output path requires such coverage under the task's testing and traceability rules.

Neither gap is acknowledged by a supplied or inspected `{fixme}` reference to the subject.
subject: requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers

rationale:
The implementation substantially covers `requirements.authoring.not_listed`, but the required negative-outcome tests do not cover every tool's output path.

### Obligations and coverage

- **Include `not_listed` for `list_files`, `ripgrep`, and `ast_grep`; use an array of `{path, reason}`; use reason `untracked`; include each relevant untracked path.** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_not_listed]` selects listing children, text matches, or structural matches and constructs the path/reason objects. Its callers in `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` apply it to all three tools. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listings_and_searches_name_untracked_files_without_their_contents]` checks the selected paths and reasons for all three.
- **Omit the field when there are none.** The empty-vector return in `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_not_listed]` and empty-field suppression in `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[render]` implement this. The tools test checks empty listing and text-search cases; `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[not_listed_comes_on_the_first_page_within_the_page_limit]` checks omission on subsequent pages without omitted entries.
- **Start on the first page; continue on subsequent pages as necessary; obey the page-size limit.** `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[with_not_listed]` prepends these entries, and `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]` uses `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[paginate]`. Both marked paging tests exercise this, including an untracked array too large for one page.
- **Include omitted entries in total counts; include them in returned counts; retain ordinary-array order; retain `not_listed` order.** `deliver` counts the combined entry stream; `render` partitions it without reordering. `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[untracked_entries_page_without_tracked_entries_or_oversized_overhead]` explicitly checks both counts and both reconstructed arrays, with zero, one, and many ordinary entries.
- **Do not disclose untracked contents; do not make untracked files evidence inputs.** The tools helper emits only path/reason objects. Listing constructors set `evidence` false, and `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[delivered]` consequently returns no evidence inputs. The tools test explicitly asserts no disclosed contents and no evidence inputs for `ripgrep`; the synthetic paging test checks empty evidence inputs across pages.
- **Do not read otherwise-excluded files to find matches; do not list them.** The helper obtains candidates through `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[DiscoverySources]/fn[untracked]`, which filters through `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[DiscoverySources]/fn[considers]` before the helper reads contents. That filter applies workspace disallow policy and `src/authoring/access.rs#fn[excluded_from_discovery]`. The tools test creates matching disallowed and generated-evidence files and checks their exclusion from all three tools' named results.

### Unacknowledged testing gap

In `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listings_and_searches_name_untracked_files_without_their_contents]`, the `ast_grep` result is checked only for its named paths and reasons: neither absence of file contents nor absence of evidence inputs is asserted. The `list_files` result likewise has no negative content/evidence assertion. The synthetic paging test checks evidence behavior for `Listing::array`, not the actual structural-search result path. These are separate tool output paths governed by the explicit MUST NOT obligations; testing the `ripgrep` delivery alone does not verify their outcomes. These prohibitions also do not qualify for the unchanged/pass-through exemption. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap.
subject: requirements.authoring.not_listed

rationale:
## Obligations and implementation

- **Every author form uses `confirm` or `once`.** `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` accepts the typed policy for all forms; `src/main.rs#fn[main]` passes it to single-subject and batch authoring. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` and `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]` resolve it before assessment.
- **An explicit flag takes precedence; otherwise use the selected configuration; otherwise use `once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends.** `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[effective_policy]` implements these four obligations. The policy-referenced tests `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_policy_defaults_to_once_without_changing_explicit_policy]` assert the defaults and precedence. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` also exercises CLI selection.
- **Under `confirm`, apply `requirements.authoring.confirmation`.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` selects confirmation rather than immediately recording the first favorable assessment. The reachable `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]` makes the corresponding decision for adaptive routing. The policy-referenced CLI tests exercise single-subject confirmation, including adaptive disagreement verification.
- **Under `once`, perform one assessment, including adaptive escalation, and record its result.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` returns the first assessment under `once`; `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]` returns one routed assessment, with escalation handled by `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[route]`. `configured_assessment` writes the result; `run_batch` stages and persists it. The policy-selection integration test checks one conversation and stdout evidence; `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` checks escalation and persisted results.
- **Reject unknown policy names as invalid arguments or configuration.** `src/config.rs#impl[AssessmentPolicy/std::str::FromStr]/fn[from_str]` rejects unknown arguments, and `src/config.rs#enum[AssessmentPolicy]` restricts deserialization. Both configuration and CLI rejection are asserted by the policy-referenced tests above.
- **Name the policy in the completion report.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` includes it in single-subject file, stdout, and batch reports. The policy-selection integration test asserts each report path.
- **Identify the policy in each usage record.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]` sets it, `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[followup_log]` copies it to subsequent conversations, and `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]` serializes it. The policy-selection integration test asserts the policy on the single-subject conversations' usage records.

## Gap

The obligation that **every author form applies confirmation under `confirm`** lacks a subject-referenced test for batch confirmation. The mandatory policy-referenced integration test exercises batch authoring only with `--policy once`; its confirmation cases are single-subject runs.

There is an appropriate existing test at `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]`: it runs `author --all --policy confirm` and asserts two conversations per subject and corresponding usage records. However, it marks only `requirements.authoring.confirmation` and `requirements.authoring.batch`, not `requirements.authoring.policy`. It needs a `{test}` reference to the subject to cover this policy-application obligation under the task's tracing rules. This is not a request to reassess the cited confirmation requirement's internal implementation or test suite.

## Judgment
The implementation substantially covers `requirements.authoring.progress`, but its required elapsed-time display has no outcome assertion in the supplied progress tests. This is an unacknowledged testing gap.

## Obligations and coverage
- **Interactive updating bar; elapsed time; percentage; finished count; total count; active count; queued count; separate true, false, FIXME, and authoring-error counts.** `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[author_all]` reaches `run_batch` and `BatchProgress`. `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[new]` enables terminal redraws, `start` installs the elapsed-time and count template, and `refresh` sets the counts and completed position. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` asserts redraws, percentage, finished/total counts, and every outcome and activity counter. The interruption test also exercises intermediate updates through its PTY helper. **Gap:** neither that terminal test nor the other marked tests asserts that elapsed time appears. The location needing coverage is `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[start]`. Checking that the elapsed-time field is rendered does not require waiting for real time to pass; the existing PTY setup already runs this code.
- **Total includes only selected assessments; current accepted records stay unchanged.** `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[select_subjects]` separates current records from selected subjects; `run_batch` passes only `subjects.len()` to `start`. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]` checks unchanged records, an empty current batch, and the one-authored/five-unchanged summary.
- **Judgments advance progress; authoring errors advance progress; progress measures completed work rather than satisfaction.** `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[completed]`, `failed`, and `refresh` count all judgments and errors equally toward position. The mixed terminal test asserts 6/6 and 100% with three true, one false, one FIXME, and one error; `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure` also covers the redirected error path.
- **Known-work inspection phases have bars, including evidence files, reference source files, reference coverage, Rust function coverage, and assessment selection.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]`, `fn[collect_references_with_progress]`, `fn[validate_references]`, `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]`, and `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[select_subjects]` emit counted updates reachable from `author_all`. The marked tests `inspection_progress_preserves_validation_and_finishes_each_phase`, `rust_function_coverage_reports_counted_progress_per_file`, and `selection_counts_definitions_and_citation_reviews_in_one_phase` assert these phase sequences. The citation-review and site-review progress tests cover their additional counted phases; `inspection_progress_reports_empty_phases_as_complete` covers empty work.
- **Current phase is labeled; completed and total checks are displayed; percentage measures that phase's checks.** `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[inspect]` resets phase position and uses the update's own length and position. `src/authoring/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[inspection_displays_counts_when_same_phase_discovers_its_total]` asserts the phase label and 50% 2/4. `percentage_does_not_round_unfinished_work_up_to_one_hundred` tests percentage boundaries.
- **Discovery and unknown-total phases use indeterminate activity.** The inspection entry point emits unknown-total discovery updates; `inspect` selects a spinner template without percentage. The same display test asserts the unknown-total phase label and absence of percentage.
- **Inspection does not change validation results; inspection does not invoke inference.** The progress callback only updates display state. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[inspection_progress_preserves_validation_and_finishes_each_phase]` compares validation outcomes with and without progress for valid and invalid repositories. The batch terminal tests assert exactly six assessment requests, while the empty/error PTY cases operate without an inference server.
- **Enabled reports remain readable alongside progress.** `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[println]` routes terminal diagnostics above the bar and redirected diagnostics to ordinary stderr. The mixed terminal test checks default false/FIXME/error reports; `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]` covers verbose rationale output. `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` covers redirected reporting.
- **Interrupted batches retain actual progress; unstarted assessments are not finished.** `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[finish]` refreshes actual counts and abandons rather than completes an interrupted bar. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[interrupted_terminal_progress_keeps_unstarted_work_incomplete]`, through `fn[assert_interruption_stops_the_batch]`, checks partial updates, Stopped, absence of 100% and 6/6, retained writes, cancellation, and unstarted work.
- **Empty batches clear the display; early errors clear the display.** `run_batch` returns through `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress/Drop]/fn[drop]`. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[empty_batches_and_early_errors_clear_the_terminal_display]` checks final-screen cleanup for empty, configuration-error, and discovery-error cases.
- **Redirected stderr retains plain reports without terminal controls; TERM=dumb does likewise.** `BatchProgress::new` disables the bar in either case. `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure`, `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose`, and `dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics` assert plain diagnostics and absence of controls.
- **NO_COLOR disables color; NO_COLOR does not disable supported-terminal progress.** `src/authoring/progress.rs#fn[progress_style]` removes color styles independently of terminal selection. The mixed terminal test asserts redraw escapes but no color escapes; `tests/authoring_batch.rs#impl[Fixture]/fn[run_in_pty_with_args]` supplies NO_COLOR alongside forced color.
- **Stdout completion summary stays unchanged; exit-status rules stay unchanged.** The mixed terminal, verbose terminal, redirected reporting, dumb-terminal, unchanged-record, and interruption tests assert the appropriate summaries and success/failure outcomes while exercising progress. These also cover the subject's application of `requirements.authoring.batch` and `requirements.authoring.reporting` without reassessing those requirements independently.

## Obligations and coverage

`requirements.authoring.read_denial` requires: (1) an explicit policy-denied request returns a tool error, (2) that error names the path, (3) it explains the reason, (4) no evidence input is added, (5) assessment continues, (6) discovery omits denied entries, (7) search omits denied entries, (8) untracked candidates are reported under `requirements.authoring.not_listed`, and (9–10) malformed arguments and ordinary read failures return explanatory tool errors.

- Obligations 1–5 are implemented by `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`: dispatch errors become error results, without extending pending evidence, and the conversation loop continues. Reachable policy checks in `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` produce path-and-reason diagnostics. Coverage includes `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_read_through_a_symlink_leaving_the_project_returns_an_error_to_the_model]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_untracked_reads_return_an_untracked_error_and_the_assessment_continues]`, and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_denied_read_returns_an_error_and_its_assessment_continues]`.
- Obligations 6–7 are implemented by access filtering in `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[list_files]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[walk_sources]`, reached through `dispatch_paged`. The latter is used by both `search` and `structural`. Tests include `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not]`.
- Obligation 8 is applied by `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` through `with_not_listed`. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listings_and_searches_name_untracked_files_without_their_contents]` checks listing, text-search, and structural-search reporting, but the implementation has the gap below.
- Obligations 9–10 are handled by argument validation and error propagation in `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[read]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]`, followed by `converse`'s error-result branch. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[malformed_and_failed_reads_return_to_the_model_and_the_assessment_continues]` exercises malformed requests, missing files/selectors, and invalid ranges. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[operating_system_permission_failures_are_ordinary_read_failures]` additionally checks OS permission failures.

## Unacknowledged gap

`src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_not_listed]` compares project-relative untracked filenames against the raw requested path, stripping only trailing slashes and special-casing exactly `.`. It does not resolve the requested path as the actual listing/search does through `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[project_path]` and `SourceAccess::path`.

Consequently, requesting `./src` (or an absolute in-project directory) can successfully list/search an eligible directory while omitting every untracked candidate from `not_listed`: a relative filename such as `src/draft.rs` does not start with `./src` or the absolute directory prefix. The denied candidate stays out of ordinary entries, but the required untracked reporting is not applied. This violates obligation 8; it is not a reassessment of the cited requirement's paging or serialization rules. The referenced reporting test uses only the default root path and `src`, so it does not catch this failure. No supplied or read `{fixme}` acknowledges it.

rationale:
## Obligations and implementation

The obligations of `requirements.authoring.refresh` are:

1. Every author form accepts `--missing`.
2. Every form accepts `--force`.
3. Those flags are mutually exclusive.
4. Missing-mode behavior is the default.
5. Missing mode assesses only selected subjects with missing, stale, or invalid evidence (each of these cases).
6. It preserves current records without a model call, including accepted FIXME records and current false records.
7. A false record is reassessed when its subject changes, when its inputs change, or when forced.
8. Force mode assesses every selected subject.
9. `--stdout` implies force.
10. The command reports the selected-subject skip count.
11. When nothing needs assessment, it succeeds without resolving model configuration or credentials.

The flag definitions are in `src/main.rs#enum[Command]`, reachable through the CLI type used by `src/main.rs#fn[main]`. The latter dispatches every author form and prints single-subject and batch skip counts. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]`, reachable from both marked roots, implements the single-subject current-record early return and stdout-implies-force rule. Batch dispatch reaches `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]` through `author_all_with_options` or `author_sites_with_options`. `run_batch` returns before resolving configuration when selection is empty.

`src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[select_subjects]` filters each subject category and counts skipped records; force bypasses that filter. `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[subject_is_current]` supplies the single-subject check. Both use `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[current]`, which accepts valid, accepted-FIXME, and current-false states. `src/index.rs#impl[LoadedDetailEvidence]/fn[load_path]` distinguishes missing and invalid evidence and does not classify a false record with additional validation findings as current.

## Tests and gap

The referenced tests provide substantial coverage:

- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` checks default and explicit missing modes, conflicting flags, single and batch force, stdout forcing, invalid-evidence repair, skip counts, preservation, and no-op success with unusable configuration.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]` checks missing evidence, accepted-FIXME preservation, changed-input selection, unchanged records, and no-op operation with invalid or absent configuration.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_preserves_current_false_judgments_and_reauthors_stale_ones]` checks current false preservation and reassessment after an input changes.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reauthors_a_false_judgment_when_its_reference_set_changes]` checks another changed-input case.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[site_reviews_are_authored_by_requirement_and_orphans_deleted_by_all]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` check review-specific selection and no-op paths; the latter also checks citation stdout forcing.

However, the expressly named **forced reassessment of a current false judgment** lacks a test. The force tests in `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` operate on true records; the false-record tests exercise preservation and stale-input reassessment, not force. None of the supplied subject-marked tests changes a current record to false and then forces its reassessment. This is a named case under the testing rules, even though `select_subjects` and `author_evidence_with_options` implement it with a determination-independent force bypass. It requires a test asserting a new assessment and its outcome; no testing exemption applies.

There is no supplied `{fixme}` acknowledging this testing gap.

## Finding

The reporting implementation matches the requested behavior, but the explicit obligation that verbosity **not change validation rules** lacks a test. This is an unacknowledged testing gap.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` checks that ordinary validation rejects an authored false assessment, but does not enable verbosity. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` checks verbose persistence and successful authoring exit status, but never validates the resulting evidence. Likewise, `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` compares reporting and command failure across verbosity settings, not evidence-validation outcomes. The stdout test checks evidence and usage records, not validation. Searching the authoring tests found no verbose validation test. Because the requirement explicitly preserves validation rules, the unchanged-value testing exemption does not apply. Add a test carrying `{test}` for `requirements.authoring.reporting` that validates evidence authored with verbosity enabled and asserts the applicable validation outcome.

## Obligation mapping

All implementation below is reachable from `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, including through its CLI types and calls into authoring.

| Separate obligations | Implementation | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Suppress per-subject true lines by default; show each false subject; show its false outcome; use stderr; work on terminals; work with redirected output | `src/main.rs#fn[main]`; `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[completed]` and `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[println]` | `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]`, `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]`, and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` exercise the judgment-reporting paths. |
| Retain progress counters; retain completion summaries | `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[refresh]`, `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[finish]`, and `src/main.rs#fn[main]` | Both terminal batch tests assert finished counts and summaries; the redirected batch test asserts the summary in both verbosity settings. |
| Keep FIXME notices visible; keep authoring errors visible | `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[completed]`, `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]/fn[failed]`, and `src/main.rs#fn[main]` | The mixed-judgment terminal and redirected batch tests assert FIXME and error messages. The stdout test asserts the single-subject FIXME notice. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` also asserts error visibility. |
| Retain single-subject subject metadata; backend metadata; model metadata; evidence destination; usage-record metadata | `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` constructs the outcome; `src/main.rs#fn[main]` formats it | The stdout test asserts subject/backend/model, stdout destination, and a real usage path. The verbose single-subject test asserts file-output Evidence and Usage reporting. |

The redirected batch test checks default and long-option modes, and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]` checks terminal short-option output. |

The verbose terminal batch test also checks absence of source text. |

Exit decisions remain in `src/main.rs#fn[main]` | Verbose single-subject and stdout tests assert persisted/emitted judgments and rationales, file preservation, and successful authoring status. rationale:
## Judgment

The implementation substantially satisfies `requirements.authoring.source_tools`, but its paged line-range output path lacks a test carrying the required reference to this subject. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges that gap.

## Obligations and coverage

The obligations, separated by property, map as follows (locations below name the code and representative subject-marked tests):

- **Expose `habeas`; accept exactly one form; map file/range, file/item, requirements, and definition requests to their respective evidence kinds.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` advertises and dispatches tools. `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]`, and `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[read]` define and enforce the interface. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` exercises all four forms and rejects incomplete, mixed, and unknown fields. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` checks provider-facing exposure and schema types.
- **Use outline-selector syntax.** `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]` delegates item resolution to `src/inputs.rs#impl[ParsedSource]/fn[resolve]`. The normal, nested, and missing-selector cases are exercised by `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]`. This applies the cited selector machinery rather than introducing another selector format.
- **Read working-tree content; include unstaged tracked edits; include staged new files.** `src/inputs.rs#impl[OutlineCache]/fn[parse]` reads through `src/inputs.rs#fn[read_project_file]`, while the index controls permission rather than supplying content. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]` asserts both staged and dirty contents.
- **Enforce resolved containment by default; require the requested file's index membership in Git; require the resolved target's membership in Git; omit the index requirement outside Git; report index-read failure.** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` and `src/authoring/access.rs#fn[tracked_sources]` implement these checks. Coverage includes `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outside_symlinks_are_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[git_symlink_reads_require_both_the_alias_and_target_to_be_tracked]`, `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[nested_project_uses_only_its_part_of_the_git_index]`, `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[empty_git_directory_in_an_ancestor_does_not_make_a_project_a_worktree]`, and `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_git_index_does_not_fall_back_to_untracked_access]`.
- **Exclude root `evidence/`; exclude its symlink aliases.** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` uses `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[generated_evidence_path]`. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]` covers direct and aliased reads.
- **Apply redaction to supplied sources.** Outline parsing uses `Redaction::of_file` and model text comes from redacted node text in `src/inputs.rs#impl[ParsedSource]/fn[node_range]`; declaration selections call redaction in `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]`. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[model_inputs_reads_searches_and_citation_prompts_are_redacted]` verifies application to mandatory inputs, item reads, line reads, and searches. The redaction algorithm itself belongs to the cited requirement.
- **Apply generated-output rules; apply workspace overrides; permit otherwise excluded inputs explicitly.** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[load]` and `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` integrate generated roots and path policy. Tests include `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files]`, `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[inherited_out_dir_is_ignored_and_metadata_failure_preserves_ordinary_reads]`, and `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[explicit_allow_overrides_defaults_but_disallow_wins_for_alias_targets]`.
- **Abort for denied mandatory inputs; return tool errors for denied model reads.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` propagates mandatory access failures, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` converts dispatched read failures into tool-error results and continues. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` tests mandatory denial; `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_untracked_reads_return_an_untracked_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` tests model-read denial and continuation. These are the subject's applications of the cited denial requirements.
- **Record selectors; record structural hashes; never record line-number identities.** `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_input]`, `src/inputs.rs#fn[recorded_input]`, and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[record_inputs]` produce the recorded forms. Both `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` assert their contents.
- **Interpret ranges as one-based; make endpoints inclusive; default the end to EOF; select innermost covering nodes, including plain-text line nodes; show selectors and source text; omit line numbers; record the selected outline inputs.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[read_lines]`, `src/inputs.rs#impl[ParsedSource]/fn[nodes_for_range]`, and `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_model_input]` carry this out. The two read tests just named cover zero rejection, EOF, single-line nested selection, multiple nodes, displayed text, and recorded identities. Plain-text output is also asserted in `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]`.
